chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about Al-Witr (the odd prayer) missing a man, he said: 'He makes up Al-Witr always.'

key_terms.الْوَتْر: Al-Witr (the odd prayer, typically the last prayer of the night)
key_terms.يَفُوتُ: Misses (fails to perform at its proper time)
key_terms.يَقْضِي: Makes up / performs the missed prayer (qada)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up the Witr prayer if it is missed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for missing the Witr prayer by stating one must 'make up Witr always' (yaqdi watran abadan). This indicates that while Witr is technically a confirmed Sunnah (Mustahabb Mu'akkad) in the Ja'fari school, its missed performance carries a permanent obligation of compensation, distinguishing it from other voluntary prayers that do not require qada. This ruling underscores the high status of Witr as the seal of the night prayer, linking it closely to the completion of the daily worship cycle.
